A particle moves along the \(x\)-axis so that its velocity at time \(t\) is given by
\[
v(t)=-(t+1) \sin \left(\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right) .
\]
At time \(t=0\), the particle is at position \(x=1\).
(a) Find the acceleration of the particle at time \(t=2\). Is the speed of the particle increasing at \(t=2\) ? Why or
why not?
(b) Find all times \(t\) in the open interval \(0<t<3\) when the particle changes direction. Justify your answer.
(c) Find the total distance traveled by the particle from time \(t=0\) until time \(t=3\).
(d) During the time interval \(0 \leq t \leq 3\), what is the greatest distance between the particle and the origin? Show
the work that leads to your answer.

\section*{Question 2}

A particle moves along the \(x\)-axis so that its velocity at time \(t\) is given by
\[
v(t)=-(t+1) \sin \left(\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right) .
\]
At time \(t=0\), the particle is at position \(x=1\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the acceleration of the particle at time \(t=2\). Is the speed of the particle increasing at \(t=2\) ? Why or why not?
\item[(b)] Find all times \(t\) in the open interval \(0<t<3\) when the particle changes direction. Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] Find the total distance traveled by the particle from time \(t=0\) until time \(t=3\).
\item[(d)] During the time interval \(0 \leq t \leq 3\), what is the greatest distance between the particle and the origin? Show the work that leads to your answer.
\item[(a)] \(a(2)=v^{\prime}(2)=1.587\) or 1.588
\(v(2)=-3 \sin (2)<0\)
Speed is decreasing since \(a(2)>0\) and \(v(2)<0\).
\item[(b)] \(v(t)=0\) when \(\frac{t^{2}}{2}=\pi\)
\(t=\sqrt{2 \pi}\) or 2.506 or 2.507
Since \(v(t)<0\) for \(0<t<\sqrt{2 \pi}\) and \(v(t)>0\) for \(\sqrt{2 \pi}<t<3\), the particle changes directions at \(t=\sqrt{2 \pi}\).
\item[(c)] Distance \(=\int_{0}^{3}|v(t)| d t=4.333\) or 4.334
\item[(d)] \(\int_{0}^{\sqrt{2 \pi}} v(t) d t=-3.265\)
\(x(\sqrt{2 \pi})=x(0)+\int_{0}^{\sqrt{2 \pi}} v(t) d t=-2.265\)
Since the total distance from \(t=0\) to \(t=3\) is 4.334, the particle is still to the left of the origin at \(t=3\). Hence the greatest distance from the origin is 2.265.
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{aligned} 1: & a(2) \\ 1: & \text { speed decreasing } \\ & \quad \text { with reason }\end{aligned}\right.\)
\begin{itemize}
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: t=\sqrt{2 \pi} \text { only } \\ 1: \text { justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { limits } \\ 1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2: \begin{cases}1: \pm & \text { (distance particle travels } \\ & \text { while velocity is negative) } \\ 1: & \text { answer }\end{cases}\)
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
